body:
This PR replaces the handwritten JavaScript port of `Std.Format.prettyM` with
Lean's implementation, executed in the browser through VIR. This removes a second
formatting algorithm to maintain and lets Slides use Lean's layout decisions
directly.

VIR is pinned to the published [4.35-rc4 release](https://github.com/ejgallego/lean-vir/releases/tag/4.35-rc4), matching this branch’s Lean toolchain.

Upstream main moved to Lean **4.35.0** in #84 while this was being prepared.
This branch and its local results use **4.35rc4**. Landing needs a matching VIR
4.35.0 source/runtime release, followed by rebase and qualification.

Lean returns text segments with their active annotation tags. JavaScript measures
the available pixel width, converts it to a column width for Lean, and renders
the returned segments using the existing highlighting, bindings, and interaction
code. VIR handles the typed call and conversion of the result.

Lake prepares the formatter program as a dependency of the existing asset
library, which embeds it together with VIR's runtime. The renderer publishes
these resources through the existing asset writer. Downstream decks continue to
use the ordinary `slidesMain` entry point and build command.

The formatter initializes once, asynchronously. Slides and navigation remain
usable while expressions are loading; the current selection is rendered when
formatting becomes available. Initialization failures are shown in the affected
panel or lightbox.

The added tests compare browser results with native Lean segments and tag stacks,
and cover annotations, panel/lightbox rendering, initialization, and publication.
The ordinary fixture builder writes the native corpus, so the Wasm comparisons
run as part of `lake test` and CI without a separate acceptance command.

## Reviewing the commits

This builds on #83. Until that PR lands, GitHub's combined diff also includes
its shared-rendering refactor. The [formatter-only diff](https://github.com/ejgallego/verso-slides/compare/23daa2e3eb45c5838bd7860cc21d06d5089515d7...db12f3a9bce3a4a202df0c5809b1aaf0464026ba)
contains the following three commits. We recommend reviewing them in order:

1. **Lean formatter and VIR integration**
   ([`dcc82c4`](https://github.com/ejgallego/verso-slides/commit/dcc82c49eb94bdc3d24e8734048220fd93dcad64)).
   Add the Lean `MonadPrettyFormat` instance that collects text and annotation
   tags, export the typed formatter entry point, and prepare/embed its resources
   through Lake. Wire publication and one-shot initialization into the renderer.
   This is the place to review the Lean implementation and asset/build setup.
2. **Switch browser formatting and remove the JavaScript port**
   ([`4a4af79`](https://github.com/ejgallego/verso-slides/commit/4a4af796f5467a2d957957623695b590af19bbaa)).
   Connect the existing measurement and presentation code to the Lean formatter,
   remove the JavaScript layout algorithm, and handle readiness in panels and
   lightboxes. This commit contains the browser behavior change.
3. **Tests, documentation, and downstream example**
   ([`db12f3a`](https://github.com/ejgallego/verso-slides/commit/db12f3a9bce3a4a202df0c5809b1aaf0464026ba)).
   Add native segment/tag comparisons, browser presentation and initialization
   checks, publication tests, a short integration guide, and a downstream deck
   that uses the ordinary build and rendering entry points. The browser tests use
   the existing code fixture; no custom site assembly or opt-in flag is needed.

## Size and build-time impact

Comparison of #83's JavaScript formatter with this patch, using the same demo
and Lean 4.35.0-rc4:

| Artifact | JavaScript formatter | Lean/VIR formatter |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Published demo, raw files | 3.51 MiB | 4.55 MiB |
| Published demo, gzip estimate | 1.78 MiB | 2.04 MiB |
| `pretty.js`, raw | 24.2 KiB | 12.5 KiB |
| Native demo executable | 123.05 MiB | 124.56 MiB |

The added VIR resources break down as follows:

| Added component | Raw | Gzip estimate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wasm runtime | 774.7 KiB | 186.2 KiB |
| VIR JavaScript runtime API | 116.7 KiB | 33.1 KiB |
| Formatter IR and embedded ABI metadata | 74.2 KiB | 12.5 KiB |
| Bundle manifests and package-set index | 4.0 KiB | 1.9 KiB |
| License and notice files | 99.7 KiB | 30.3 KiB |
| **Total** | **1069.4 KiB** | **264.0 KiB** |

The PrettyM program, including its descriptors, is 77.1 KiB raw /
13.7 KiB gzip; the remainder is the shared runtime and its accompanying
files. ABI metadata is embedded in the IR packages. Notices remain distributed
with the runtime; the loader fetches and verifies runtime code and program members
for initialization. Gzip figures are sums of per-file compression at level 9,
rather than measured network transfers.

| Build | JavaScript formatter | Lean/VIR formatter |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh Slides build, dependencies already built | 33.1 s | 32.4 s |
| Warm no-change build | 0.72 s | 1.14 s |

Local medians on a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370: two successful fresh application-build
samples and eight no-change samples per version, alternating old/new order.
Command: `lake --no-cache build`. Dependency libraries and the runtime are already
cached; downloads and setup are excluded. Ordinary demo extraction/highlighting
is included. Background work and OS caches are not isolated, and the fresh-build
ranges overlap; these small samples do not establish a speed improvement.
One old-baseline extraction/linker failure was retained and replayed without a
source change, and is excluded from the successful timings.

[Measurements and focused release-pair acceptance](https://github.com/ejgallego/verso-slides/tree/fd5b7ec43fe0ba9ab635790dc5ad52233d0b3084/docs/evidence/release435-adoption)
retain exact revisions, methods, raw logs and artifact identities. Native and
ordinary downstream checks plus 30 focused Chromium/Firefox cases passed with
the released runtime and regenerated program.

The revised ordinary test path also passes the complete browser suite:
[310 Chromium/Firefox checks, including the enabled formatter comparisons](https://github.com/ejgallego/verso-slides/tree/59a8ffd1f2c867a2660fe403f0ccb4971931844a/docs/evidence/ordinary-formatter-tests).
The test cleanup changes no production formatter/runtime bytes, so the footprint
measurements above still apply.
